Subject: Service vitals: April snapshot + QBR prep

Team —

I pulled the April ops snapshot and flagged a few items we need to close before the QBR readout next week. Attached is the April_OPS_Dashboard.xlsx (summary sheet + per-region tabs). High-level:

- Latency: 95th P90 increased from 240ms -> 380ms on US-West on 2027-03-28 during a promotional spike; tail latency impact was most visible for chat endpoints.
- Cost: Host-level GPU spend is up ~18% month-over-month driven by repeated unbatched reruns and lower KV cache hit rates on short prompts.
- Uptime: One 18m pager incident 2027-03-29 (routing flake) — postmortem in progress (JIRA OPS-1428).
- Usage: Daily active request volume up 27% y/y, consistent with new customer onboarding (Acme AI noted).

As part of QBR prep I want an owners matrix for each item and concrete mitigations we can commit to in the next two weeks. Initial asks:

1) Latency owner + quick mitigation (can we temporarily tighten batch timeouts / increase pool reserve?) — assignable to Jonas.
2) Cost owner + quick wins (cache policy + disable expensive reruns) — assignable to Laura.
3) Customer coordination note (we need Acme to throttle or coordinate ramp) — Grace to own communications.
4) Postmortem summary due for OPS-1428 (include timeline + RCA) — ops lead.

Please reply here with owners and 1-sentence plan by COB today. I'll assemble the readout and schedule a 45-min QBR prep on Monday.

Attachments: April_OPS_Dashboard.xlsx

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

Quick technical readout from the infra side:

- Preliminary RCA: US-West tail latency correlates with prolonged batching windows on dedicated pools when a small fraction of sessions send many short prompts (median token length < 20). The batching engine was holding open slots waiting for in-flight requests which created amplification for other requests.
- Evidence: attached latency_heatmap.png and request-level latency traces (summary in Drive).
- Immediate mitigation (safe): temporarily reduce max-batch-wait to 6ms for affected pool and increase min-reserve by 2 GPUs for 48 hours. This should cut the 95th by ~90ms based on replay tests.
- Medium-term: adjust batching policy to favor prefix-hits and implement a KV-cache fallback to reduce repeated context reconstruction.

I'll push a canary of the config tonight and report numbers in the morning. ETA for config rollback/confirm: 24h.

Attachments: latency_heatmap.png

Jonas
Director, Serving Runtime

Attached is a quick cost slice (see "top_drivers" tab in April_OPS_Dashboard.xlsx). TL;DR:

- Top driver #1: repeated developer reruns and low cache hit rate on short prompts (~22% hit).
- Top driver #2: bursted dedicated pool usage for a small set of customers (~12% of spend attributed to two accounts).

Proposed quick actions (safe to implement within 72h):
- Enable prefix caching for short prompt patterns (audit to ensure no PII exposure).
- Enforce a soft rate-limit on reruns from internal/dev keys and flag heavy reruns for account owners.
- Short-term: increase batch target slightly for large seq workloads and lower for short prompt flows to avoid amplification.

I'll coordinate with finance to get a short cost-offset proposal for the QBR slides. Thanks Jonas for the latency plan — tagging you on the canary.

Laura Bennett
Head of Cost & Business Analytics
